title: PhysicalPropertyResourceAttributes

name.title: Physical Property Name
name.description:
Name of the physical property. Example: 'ElectronicBandGap'.

- **Type**: string.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: REQUIRED in implementations.
  - **Query**: MUST be a queryable property with support for all mandatory filter features.
- **Examples**:
  - `"ElectronicBandGap"`
  - `"TotalEnergy"`
  - `"ElectronicDensityOfStates"`

iri.title: Internationalized Resource Identifier
iri.description:
Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) pointing to a definition, typically within a larger, ontological framework.

- **Type**: string (URI format).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be empty string.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property.
- **Examples**:
  - `"https://w3id.org/emmo/domain/electrochemistry#electrochemistry_43cd6e14_dd43_41b5_b5b4_4db94403c9e8"`

type.title: Physical Property Type
type.description:
Type categorization of the physical property. Example: an 'ElectronicBandGap' can be 'direct' or 'indirect'.

- **Type**: string.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property with support for all mandatory filter features.
- **Examples**:
  - `"direct"`
  - `"indirect"`
  - `"kinetic"`
  - `"potential"`

contribution_type.title: Contribution Type
contribution_type.description:
Type of contribution to the physical property. Hence, only applies to contributions instances. Example: 'TotalEnergy' may have contributions like 'kinetic', 'potential', etc.

- **Type**: string.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property.
  - **Note**: Should only be set for contribution instances, not top-level properties.
- **Examples**:
  - `"kinetic"`
  - `"potential"`
  - `"exchange"`
  - `"correlation"`

label.title: Physical Property Label
label.description:
Label for additional classification of the physical property. Example: an 'ElectronicBandGap' can be labeled as 'DFT' or 'GW' depending on the methodology used to calculate it.

- **Type**: string.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property.
- **Examples**:
  - `"DFT"`
  - `"GW"`
  - `"DMFT"`
  - `"experimental"`

value.title: Physical Property Value
value.description:
The main property data value. The specific type and structure depend on the property.

- **Type**: varies (number, array, object).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations as structure varies by property type.
  - **Query**: MAY be queryable depending on property type and implementation.
- **Examples**:
  - `1.5` (for a scalar band gap in eV)
  - `[1.2, 1.8, 2.1]` (for multiple values)
  - Complex structures for band structures, DOS, etc.

is_derived.title: Is Derived Property
is_derived.description:
Flag indicating whether the physical property is derived from other physical properties. Distinction between directly parsed and derived physical properties: directly parsed properties come from simulation output files, derived properties are calculated from other properties.

- **Type**: boolean.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: REQUIRED in implementations.
  - **Query**: MUST be a queryable property with support for all mandatory filter features.
- **Examples**:
  - `false` (directly parsed from simulation output)
  - `true` (calculated from other properties)

physical_property_ref.title: Physical Property Reference
physical_property_ref.description:
Reference to the PhysicalProperty from which this property was derived. If populated, 'is_derived' should be true.

- **Type**: string (reference/ID to another PhysicalProperty).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property for traversing derivation chains.
- **Examples**:
  - `"property_123"`
  - `"total_energy_dft_001"`

is_scf_converged.title: SCF Convergence Status
is_scf_converged.description:
Flag indicating whether the physical property is converged after a self-consistent field (SCF) process.

- **Type**: boolean.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: SHOULD be a queryable property for filtering converged results.
- **Examples**:
  - `true` (SCF converged)
  - `false` (SCF not converged)
  - `null` (not applicable or unknown)

self_consistency_ref.title: Self Consistency Reference
self_consistency_ref.description:
Reference to the SelfConsistency section that defines the numerical settings used to converge the physical property.

- **Type**: string (reference/ID to SelfConsistency settings).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: MAY be queryable for linking to convergence parameters.
- **Examples**:
  - `"scf_settings_001"`
  - `"convergence_params_dft"`

entity_ref.title: Entity Reference
entity_ref.description:
Reference to the entity that the physical property refers to. Examples: macroscopic system vs specific atom in unit cell.

- **Type**: string (reference/ID to Entity).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be `null`.
  - **Query**: MAY be queryable for entity-specific filtering.
- **Examples**:
  - `"system_001"`
  - `"atom_fe_1"`
  - `"unit_cell"`

contributions.title: Property Contributions
contributions.description:
Shallow list of contributions to the physical property. Does not necessarily entail a full partitioning. Each contribution is itself a PhysicalProperty.

- **Type**: array of PhysicalProperty references.
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations, i.e., MAY be empty array.
  - **Query**: MAY be queryable for exploring property decompositions.
  - **Note**: Contributions should not have nested contributions.
- **Examples**:
  - `["kinetic_energy_001", "potential_energy_001"]` (for TotalEnergy)
  - `["exchange_energy_001", "correlation_energy_001"]` (for XCEnergy)

metadata.title: Property Metadata
metadata.description:
Additional metadata fields that may vary by property type and implementation.

- **Type**: object (flexible schema).
- **Requirements/Conventions**:
  - **Support**: OPTIONAL support in implementations.
  - **Query**: Implementation-dependent queryability.
- **Examples**:
  - Units, dimensions, coordinate systems
  - Calculation parameters
  - Visualization settings

description:
Physical property resource attributes following OPTIMADE specification patterns. Represents computational output properties with support for derivation chains, contributions, and metadata.

## Property Types
This base schema supports various physical property types including:
- Electronic properties (band gaps, eigenvalues, density of states)
- Energy properties (total, kinetic, potential energies)
- Force properties (total forces, stress tensors)
- Optical properties (permittivity, absorption spectra)
- Thermodynamic properties (temperature, pressure, entropy)

## Relationships
- **Derivation**: Properties can reference other properties via `physical_property_ref`
- **Contributions**: Complex properties can be decomposed into constituent parts
- **Convergence**: SCF-computed properties track convergence status

## Implementation Notes
- Implementations should validate that `contribution_type` is only set for contribution instances
- Contributions should not contain nested contributions
- The `value` field structure varies significantly by property type
- Plotting and visualization capabilities are supported but not part of this schema
